plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks crowned with huge golden-yellow flower heads that follow the sun across the sky. In early August, fields across the northern plains glow in endless rows of gold, humming with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early autumn (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Great Plains of North America and sunflower fields across central and southern Europe
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower but hundreds to thousands of tiny florets arranged in spirals that follow Fibonacci numbers.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds topped with slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue blossoms. In the warm days of early August, lavender fields in southern France hum with pollinators and perfume the air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (roughly late June to August) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Provence, France, and Mediterranean-climate gardens throughout Europe
plants.funFact: The name lavender is thought to come from the Latin lavare, meaning to wash, because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small Australian tree that bursts into fluffy golden pompom blossoms at the end of winter. Its glowing clusters light up the bushland of southeastern Australia and signal that spring is on its way.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (about July to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated each year on September 1.
